A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MEMENTO. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and presentation.

before.justification: v2 reports original TSP and CVRP experiments, scaling measurements, feature ablations, and training analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds augmentation, runtime-budget, and training-budget evaluations.

M1.justification: The adopted method retains per-node memory retrieval, the same features and MLP-based additive logit corrections, budget-weighted training, and zero-shot COMPASS combination. Appendix I expands retrieval documentation without establishing a change to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same TSP/CVRP benchmark populations, including uniform 100–200-node instances, 500-node evaluations, and the existing size-scaling coverage. The new augmentation and budget experiments change procedures within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 9 adds POMO to the instance-size runtime comparison previously shown only for EAS and MEMENTO. Comparator membership in the retained main benchmarks is unchanged; newly cited Meta-SAGE and learned tree-search work are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 adds eightfold symmetry-augmented evaluation and equal-time budgets based on EAS runtime. Appendix K crosses training budgets of 100, 200, and 300 attempts with inference budgets from 50 to 1600. These substantially extend evaluation design while retaining the original fixed-attempt benchmark.

E4.justification: v3 adds training-budget sensitivity analysis, budget-dependent update heatmaps, and an overhead comparison against POMO. Conversely, Figure 9 reduces six feature-ablation configurations to four, grouping the final three feature additions and removing two intermediate configurations.

E5.justification: The standard-deviation discussion and shading associated with Figure 5 are retained. Neither version reports run/seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests that establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original main benchmark scores and parallel/sequential-attempt table are numerically retained. v3 adds substantial results in Tables 6, 7, 9, and 13, including MEMENTO beating EAS on six of eight reported optimality gaps under equal-time budgets. Existing reported runtimes also change: MEMENTO(COMPASS) on TSP100 changes from 45 seconds in v2 Table 2 to 32 seconds in v3 Table 5.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds limited analytical resource accounting, deriving approximately 8 MB for its TSP100 memory example and discussing storage and processing-cost dependencies. The MDP objectives, logit equations, training loss, and Appendix F REINFORCE derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The title and abstract focus more specifically on routing, and the conclusion removes the explicit claim of applicability to a very large set of problems. The central adaptation, scalability, zero-shot combination, and 11-of-12-task claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds discussion of parallel-batch memory bottlenecks and interprets training-budget robustness with an explicit tuning-bias qualification. Its conclusion removes v2's caveats about poor base policies and distant test distributions, replacing them with proposed COMPASS-specific training.

D1.justification: v3 adds float32 storage accounting, memory-processing workload details, and a more explicit alternative retrieval description; existing hyperparameter values are retained. Appendix D replaces two checkpoint-link disclosures with anonymization placeholders, although the main repository link remains available in the text.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Meta-SAGE by Son et al. and learned tree search by Macfarlane et al. It also removes the explicit assertion that MEMENTO scales better and achieves higher performance than FER, while retaining the architectural distinction.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, wording is tightened across the abstract, method description, and conclusion, and budget terminology is clarified. Acknowledgements and Appendices I–K are added, but the main section sequence and much of the existing narrative remain.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes the displays: v2 Figure 3 becomes Table 1, and the combined Figure 7 is split into Tables 3–4 and redisplayed scaling plots. It adds a front-page overview, new appendix tables and heatmaps, and enlarges Figures 8–9 using logarithmic relative-tour-length axes and revised legends.

improvement.justification: v2's fixed-attempt comparisons involve unequal runtimes; v3's equal-time and augmented comparisons better test the efficiency claim, while budget sensitivity and resource explanations strengthen its support. These gains outweigh the reduced feature-ablation detail, removed failure caveats, and stale checkpoint placeholders, but leave the central method and original benchmark evidence largely unchanged.
